label: UniFi Dream Machine
description: UniFi Dream Machine (UDM) - 1x 1G RJ45 WAN + 4x 1G RJ45 LAN, no PoE. WiFi 5; 26 W max.
notes:
Port census from the vendor datasheet, 'Networking interface': (4) LAN GbE RJ45 ports, (1) WAN GbE RJ45 port; no SFP and no PoE on this model. Max. power consumption 26 W. The tech-spec page (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm, 608,032 B, read 2026-11-18) prints no networking-interface row, so the datasheet is the source of the counts.
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, 747,030 B, read 2026-11-19, three-page PDF with a text layer) says "Power method: Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 0.6A Max., 50/60 Hz; Power supply: AC/DC, internal, 50 W"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so WAN / LAN 1 / LAN 2 / LAN 3 / LAN 4 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

Layer 2: Ubiquiti's controller device database classifies this SKU as a switch - https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, read 2026-11-21) lists UDM deviceCapabilities GATEWAY, SWITCH, ACCESS_POINT, NETWORK_APPLICATION, CONTROLLER, APPLICATION_MODE, HAS_CLIENTS and draws its panel as `01 02 03 04 __ 05`: four LAN sockets and the WAN set apart. The datasheet this row already cites, https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, 747,030 B, three pages with a text layer, read 2026-11-21), prints "Networking interface: (4) LAN: GbE RJ45 ports / (1) WAN: GbE RJ45 port" and, in Software, "VLAN 802.1Q"; the tech-spec URL https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm (HTTP 200, 608,032 B, read 2026-11-21) carries the model name but no specification table - the unknown-slug control 307s to the 609,911 B techspecs front page - so the datasheet is the source here. While the row shipped without `l2-forward` its four LAN sockets were routed interfaces: `switchport access vlan 10` was answered with "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability", and two hosts on LAN 1 and LAN 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP ("not addressed to this device"). The WAN socket stays a separate routed port - it is the one the diagram sets apart and the only one the datasheet calls WAN - so it is not part of the bridge and takes an address as before.
